title: Ghost Bus Tour to benefit library foundation

content:
GREEN RIVER -- History, mystery and a little paranormal activity will come together this Halloween season as the Sweetwater County Library Foundation introduces the Ghost Ride Haunted History Tour, its newest fundraising experience.

The one-night-only event will take guests on a guided journey by some of Green River's historic locations inside a decorated party bus, sharing stories of the community's past, local legends and possible paranormal encounters along the way.

Event Details

What: Ghost Ride Haunted History Bus Tour

When: Friday, Oct. 30, 2026

Departure Times: Every hour from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m.

Where: Downtown Green River, departing from Expedition Island

Tickets: $25 per person

Capacity: Only 15 guests per departure

Duration: Approximately 50 minutes · Tickets Online: www.SweetwaterMazes.com

All proceeds from the Ghost Ride Haunted History Bus Tour will benefit the Sweetwater County Library System, helping support library programs, services and resources for residents throughout Sweetwater County.

Hosted by the Foundation's Ghost Walk Crew and Stellar Paranormal, the approximately 50-minute tour will feature historical storytelling and an opportunity to experience real paranormal investigation equipment used by the team during its investigations.

"This is such a fun opportunity to bring together local history, a little mystery and a chance to experience the paranormal this Halloween, all while raising money for our libraries," said Lisa Frint, Executive Director of the Sweetwater County Library Foundation.

Sami Doak, owner of Stellar Paranormal and tour host says,

“I’m so excited to be volunteering my time to help lead the tour,” said Sami Doak, owner of Stellar Paranormal and tour host. “Through Stellar Paranormal, I love sharing our local history and a little spooky fun, so getting to do that while supporting our libraries makes it even better.”

According to Doak, all proceeds go toward supporting libraries and programs like summer and winter reading.

“As board president of the Sweetwater County Library Foundation, I couldn’t be happier to be part of it,” Doak said.

The tour will begin and end at Expedition Island, taking guests past several notable downtown locations, including the historic Bar Row, Flaming Gorge Way, East Second North, the Green River Cemetery and the Sweetwater County Library.

Newly added to the tour is a special stop at Three Owls Bookshop, one of downtown Green River's newest businesses located in the old Mercantile. Guests will have an opportunity to browse the shop's collection, hear about the history of the location, and receive a special surprise gift.

“Three Owls Bookshop is so excited to partner with the Sweetwater County Library Foundation for the Haunted History Bus Tours,” said Kaitlin Pauli, Owner of Three Owls Bookshop. “As a small, locally owned bookstore, we believe that the heart of a community lies in its stories, and what better way to celebrate that than by exploring the history and hauntings of our very own downtown Green River.”

Pauli expressed how honored the shop is to be part of an event that supports local libraries, celebrates local history, and brings the community together in such “a fun and memorable way.”

“We can’t wait to see everyone on October 30,” Pauli said.

The event is being organized in partnership with Between the Lines, which is providing the bus transportation, and the Sweetwater County Historical Museum, which assisted with providing historical information for the tour.

The Ghost Ride is being held in conjunction with the Foundation's Twisted Tales Haunted Maze & Candy Crawl, which is happening Oct. 30 through Nov. 1 at Expedition Island Pavilion. Both events are part of the Foundation's Halloween fundraising efforts.
